material_findings.reasoning: The three named classes describe manifest-error detail records, not the complete exception/report domain. In tagged bagit-python v1.9.0, _validate_entries (860–908) raises BagValidationError carrying ChecksumMismatch details; ChecksumMismatch is not the thrown exception. BagValidationError (947–961) can have an empty details list; _validate_structure_data_dir and _validate_structure_manifests (729–756) use that form. _open (322–369) also raises BagError for missing bagit.txt, unsupported declarations and decoding failures; FileNormalizationConflict is separate. The current immutable commit 4bd2713cedbe1f8e634567c20ef0dded9622011d, src/bagit/__init__.py, retains the same structure. A catch keyed only to the three detail types omits ordinary malformed packages and V1 catches the wrong type. The explicit complete-vocabulary claim and applicable-as-written/triply-confirmed oracle are false, even though the proposal is honestly unexecuted.

candidate.passage: full manifest validation over SHA-256+SHA-512 defaults at ingest; V1 BagIt round-trip; BagIt structural+fixity contract

material_findings.original_obligation: O2 selected mechanism domain applicability; O6 meaningful negative validation
material_findings.reasoning: RFC 8493 §2.3 requires every payload manifest to list every payload file once. bagit-python v1.9.0 _load_manifests (663–723) combines manifest entries by path; _validate_completeness (839–858) checks the union of manifest paths against filesystem paths; _calc_hashes (1111–1124) checks only the algorithms present for each path. Static counterexample: a valid-looking 1.0 bag with data/a and data/b, manifest-sha256 listing only a and manifest-sha512 listing only b, both with correct digests and correct optional oxum, has a complete union and matching stored checksums but violates the RFC in both manifests. The selected full-validation path has no separate per-manifest completeness check. The final credits it with the structural contract and proposes only ordinary bags plus a byte mutation, which does not expose this gap. This is an applicability omission for untrusted donor bags, not a claim that all bags or normal make_bag output fail. The current immutable module has the same union-based logic.

candidate.passage: exit 0 clean → continue, 1 infected → quarantine, 2 error/oversize/encrypted → quarantine

material_findings.original_obligation: O2 governing defaults/exceptions; O5 malware/quarantine separation; O6 accurate negative fixtures
material_findings.reasoning: The primary manpage return codes mean no virus found / virus found / errors occurred; they do not assign every oversize or encrypted file to code 2. Its --max-filesize documentation says oversized files are skipped and assumed clean. --alert-exceeds-max and --alert-encrypted default off. Released scanner code returns CL_CLEAN for over-limit files without the heuristic option; with it enabled the result is CL_VIRUS, which clamscan maps to exit 1. --move operates on infected/found files, not on arbitrary code-2 errors. Merely setting caps, asserting spellings, and rebinding to a manpage does not configure a skip-detection gate. Thus the specified exit-0 continuation can ingest an unscanned file, and the code-2 quarantine placement is not implemented by --move. P1 separately quarantines encrypted ZIP at preflight and reduces that one case; it does not cure the size-limit route or the asserted mapping. V3 repeats the same erroneous oracle.

candidate.passage: 1.0 tightened from 0.97; single-manifest 0.97 bags are repair candidates, not valid 1.0

material_findings.original_obligation: O2 specification/version semantics; O4 false correction audit; O6 discriminating interoperability fixture
material_findings.reasoning: RFC 8493 §2.3 explicitly permits one payload manifest. The changes section says older versions allowed a payload file to occur in only one of multiple manifests; 1.0 requires it in every manifest. That change invalidates disjoint/incomplete multiple-manifest layouts, not single-manifest packaging. A bag labelled 0.97 is not thereby a 1.0-labelled bag, and a profile may require declaration migration, but the final repeatedly treats the single-manifest layout as the broken rule and makes it a negative fixture. A conformant one-manifest 1.0 bag is valid; a conformant 0.97 bag need not acquire a second manifest to repair this rule. bagit-python itself accepts the legacy version range. This is a specific false structural correction, not a demand that the archive accept all legacy headers.

candidate.passage: SHA-512-only default recommended ... halves manifest size/hash time for large AV; m6 dual-hash cost accepted

material_findings.original_obligation: O2 types/units/implementation costs; O4 supported user-decision rationale
material_findings.reasoning: Neither RFC default guidance nor source code supports the promised factor of two. SHA-256 hex digests have 64 characters and SHA-512 have 128; removing SHA-256 from a dual set removes about one third of digest characters, with path/header overhead making the overall fraction workload-dependent. _calculate_file_hashes (1127–1147 in v1.9.0; 1160–1181 in the current module) reads each file once and feeds all requested hashers. Eliminating one algorithm can save CPU work but does not halve file I/O, and SHA-256/SHA-512 CPU throughput depends on platform. The performance promise is unmeasured and used to justify a default for large-media donors. The SHA-512-only choice is standards-compatible and remains a legitimate option; the claimed cost justification is unsupported. The critic m6 does not supply a benchmark or make the factor true.

candidate.passage: every payload file in every payload manifest; BagIt validate ... RFC 8493 validity; V1 ... Discriminates 1.0-rule compliance

material_findings.original_obligation: O2 tool applicability against selected contract; O6 distinguishing validation
material_findings.reasoning: The final states the correct every-file/every-manifest rule but assumes pinned bagit==1.9.0 implements it. Its _load_manifests merges entries by path, _validate_completeness compares only the union of manifest entries with payload paths, and _calc_hashes computes only the algorithms present for each entry. Two payload files split between otherwise correctly hashed sha256 and sha512 manifests pass these static conditions despite violating RFC 8493 §2.3. The proposed second implementation is useful, but the selected normal dual-/single-hash fixtures and byte mutation do not exercise this malformed multiple-manifest case, and the supposed legacy single-manifest fixture tests the wrong boundary. A source-level capability check was available and consequential.

This is a scoped implementation qualification, not evidence that the proposed app cannot add its own audit records.

The upstream change was to include/exclude byte signatures while building signatures; -doubleup is a roy build option, not a general runtime switch that a donor must pass to sf. The actual discovery that identification and validation differ is sound.

Released ClamAV 1.5.0 libfreshclam/libfreshclam.c lines 748, 775, 849, 983 and 1009 recommend no more than once an hour in rate-limit/block handling. The freshclam manual defaults to 12 checks/day and accepts 1–50 checks/day; it does not establish a universal four-per-hour cap. The stated ceiling can permit more frequent requests than upstream guidance and should be bound to the actual update configuration. This is a minor operational-source qualification: the final separately fails closed on stale DB or updater failure, so it does not itself license ingest with an obsolete detector.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept SNSD correction; qualify license trigger
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: Primary MinIO README requires distributed erasure coding for named protection features; second copy is distinct. AGPL network modifications need §13 qualification.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept PyPI pin amendment; reject auto-fetch implication
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: PyPI has 1.9.0 and its artifact hash. validate_fetch permits file URL syntax without retrieving it. Unsafe paths remain app guards.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept softened Archivematica demotion and removal of 50GB claim
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: A packaging defect is not architectural unfitness; issue closure and updated packages make the final revisit-after-fix framing stale.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept primary return-code retrieval; reject inferred oversize/encrypted routing
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: The manpage proves 0/1/2 meanings, not that limits or encryption always return 2. Released defaults contradict that inference.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept weaker server-bagged attestation and v1 encrypted-resupply choice
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: The literal donor-attestation-absent report sentence is useful; password handoff stays a future policy choice.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept pre-bag triage and normalization row
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: Bag validation does not retroactively audit filename repair performed before manifests. Mapping and event retention are needed. Encoding policy qualification remains.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept named writer and portability oracle
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: Explicit single-writer queue and config-only scratch endpoint comparison make the tests more discriminating; they remain unexecuted. OCFL alone does not implement the queue.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept SWORD spec and capable-server condition
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: The v3 BagIt packaging section exists; mediated deposit is a server capability, not a universal client assumption.
Workflow pattern is supported without certifying the old donor code against RFC 8493.
An exporter or log integration is app work; freshclam is not presented as a native Prometheus service.
Derived-index claim now has a drop/rebuild/diff oracle. That is stronger than merely naming an index as derived.
veraPDF is a conformance validator, not an all-PDF preservation guarantee.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Reject factor-of-two cost rationale; accept hash user decision
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: The critic cost claim lacks a measurement and ignores single-pass shared reads and unequal digest widths.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept local PREMIS accession vocabulary qualification
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: Declared local event types are different from claiming an OAIS function is a universal PREMIS type.
Signed-manifest/transparency sufficiency remains a threat-model question rather than an achieved provenance guarantee.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept donor identity/auth as a product decision
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: Receipt identity must bind attestation; SWORD mediation does not supply donor-web authentication by itself.
Rights entities, quarantine retention and access controls are real inputs; no legal policy is invented.
Large-transfer handling is retained as proposed application capability, not an executed storage guarantee.
Report content is concrete while dashboard/email/donor visibility is an explicit owner decision.
The broader P dispositions are reasonable. Independent single-manifest false correction contradicts the blanket audit.

criticism_dispositions.assessment: Accept added concurrency, parser and rebuild discrimination; qualify V1/V3/V6
criticism_dispositions.reasoning: Normal interop tests do not catch split manifests; scanner skip conditions and OpenRefine non-replayable edits need correct oracles. No runtime execution is claimed.

plan_dispositions.assessment: ZIP stays as serialization of a BagIt directory; legacy staff bagging reports absent donor attestation. Exactly code adoption versus interface rebuild, SWORD-capable existing server, encrypted resupply and possible later password handoff remain options. Unsafe-path policy is not attributed solely to the library.

plan_dispositions.disposition: Already-covered plus correction and hash user decision
plan_dispositions.assessment: Fixity/provenance distinction is retained, as are artifact pinning and remote-fetch policy. SHA-512-only is a standards-compatible alternative, but should be read as a changed default awaiting user choice, not literal retention of every SHA-256 verification. The single-manifest rejection is false (N1-M2), and the factor-of-two cost justification is unsupported (N1-M3).

plan_dispositions.clause: P3: Extract to the archive folder and update a database.
plan_dispositions.assessment: The staged workflow, derived index, single-writer serialization, second copy and format-validation routing materially improve the thin plan. SNSD is no longer confused with replication or WORM. The initial malware exit routing remains unsafe (N1-M1); selected BagIt validity is over-credited (N1-M4).

plan_dispositions.clause: P4: Let staff edit metadata after import.
plan_dispositions.assessment: Original post-import capability is retained through review, staging repair, revalidation, new OCFL version and PREMIS event. No unsupported assertion that all metadata must be embedded is adopted. Required fields, role/rights and edit authority remain user inputs. Replay qualification is N1-m5.

Original names are retained with mapping and pre-bag collision/decoding reports. Suggested suffix is explicitly proposed, not silently enacted. Non-UTF-8 policy is a stricter profile, not universally forbidden by BagIt; see N1-m4.

plan_dispositions.clause: P6: Test with three good packages.
plan_dispositions.assessment: The three good packages stay. V1–V8 cover malformed packages, malware, provenance, repair, concurrent version commits, portability and index rebuild. None is executed. Wrong V1/V3 boundaries are explicit findings rather than a general rejection of the suite.

validation_assessment.reasoning: Three good uploads through report/history remain useful. Under-an-hour on a reference VM is a target, not measured performance.

validation_assessment.status: Proposed; partly discriminating, wrong structural boundary
validation_assessment.reasoning: Second implementation is useful; one-byte mismatch and normal dual-/SHA-512 bags do not detect split manifests. The single-manifest legacy failure condition is N1-M2; exact manifest-line output remains asserted at build.

Versions, dedup, corruption and root/head mismatch are useful. Exactly one initial commit wins through the explicit queue; loser may retry, so the expected first-attempt result must be separated from eventual two commits.

validation_assessment.status: Proposed; meaningful fixtures, materially wrong routing premise
validation_assessment.reasoning: EICAR, limits, nested/password containers, parser formats and stale DB are discriminating if each skipped/non-scanned outcome is distinguished. The stated 0/1/2 size/encryption route is false (N1-M1).

validation_assessment.status: Proposed; meaningful fixity/provenance distinction and honest open countercase
validation_assessment.reasoning: Pre-manifest substitution can verify; post-manifest substitution fails. Event/attestation evidence can report the difference in custody, not magically establish actual donor bytes without trusted evidence. Server-bagged wording is concrete; signature/transparency threat model is unresolved.
TIFF/PPT/Broadcast-WAVE fixtures record both ID and validator results, with generic PDF separate from PDF/A. No current full-format matrix was run.

validation_assessment.status: Proposed; useful repair audit with replay qualification
validation_assessment.reasoning: CSV cleaning, staff review, revalidation and events test silent-edit risk. OpenRefine extraction does not reproduce all single-cell edits (N1-m5).

validation_assessment.status: Proposed and conditional; meaningful portability oracle
validation_assessment.reasoning: SWORD requires a capable existing server; S3 endpoint/credential/config-only swap plus the same validation subset can falsify portability. Object-lock/credential differences are measured targets, not proven equivalence.
Dropping/rebuilding and comparing the index tests whether preservation events and objects really suffice, unlike checking only a successful index write.

N1.grade_limits: FAIL is established by the enumerated primary-grounded defects; no positive full-quality certification is made. All six axes, every P clause, every proposed validation, all observed criticism and mapped stage preservation were reviewed. Relevant consequential selected-mechanism source coverage is complete at the requested research level; unchosen deployment inputs and unexecuted proposals remain explicitly unresolved. The previously inaccessible FAQ was retrieved through the official source repository, and released freshclam code independently resolves the cadence detail.

method_clues.mapping: N2=control, N1=treatment, as disclosed in exact input-map. Directory names and candidate text reveal methods. No complete blindness is claimed.
method_clues.independence: Fresh evaluator; no other case, evaluator answer, premium reference or provider history accessed; no nested worker or candidate feedback.

comparative_assessment: Both arms have source-grounded material FAIL with complete six-axis and relevant selected-mechanism primary coverage. Neither is a full-quality pass or eligible for a quality/speed/cost comparison. Their failures differ: N2 has wrong exception/alert oracles and validator completeness; N1 has unsafe skipped-scan routing, a false legacy BagIt correction, unsupported hash-cost rationale, validator completeness and a lost quarantine-release condition. Two FAIL grades do not establish equal quality, and no winner or faster-FAIL advantage follows.

No runtime is available in candidate stages; candidate no-runtime declarations are honest. Local evaluator parsing/hash verification and primary retrieval are assessment operations, not product tests.
Current product versions/prices and local legal/retention policy not adopted by these research finals are not silently converted into required production research.
